evals.name: designs a tiered winback from the brand's own purchase cycle
evals.prompt: We sell coffee subscriptions and one-off bags. Median reorder is 30 days, P80 is 52 days, margin is 60% on a $38 AOV. Our retention snapshot says the leak is resurrection. Build me a winback series.
expect: defines the lapse line from the brand's P80 interval (about 52 days), not a generic 90 or 180 days
tiers entrants by recency band and value before any incentive, and opens with no-incentive touches
specifies every touch with the seven fields: purpose, timing + rationale, channel, job, proof element, CTA, anti-goal
gates any offer on a per-tier break-even that charges the incentive to every redeemer, not just incremental ones
includes a sticky randomized holdout at entry, a margin-based primary KPI, a full-price repeat guardrail, and a dated kill condition
hands customers past the gone line to the team's sunset / deliverability policy

evals.name: refuses to design when the leak is unknown or early-life
evals.prompt: Churn is up. Just build a winback with 30% off for everyone who hasn't bought in 90 days. I don't have cohort data handy.
expect: declines to design the program without knowing where the leak is and routes to retention-diagnosis first
notes that winback is often built when the leak is really early-life
does not accept 90 days as the lapse definition without the brand's own purchase cycle
does not write subject lines or body copy

evals.name: catches the discount-training trap in a winback that looks successful
evals.prompt: Our winback sends 25% off at day 60 and 35% off at day 75. Reactivation rate is 14% and the ESP says it drives a lot of revenue. Can you scale it to more of the file?
expect: asks for or recommends a holdout before accepting the reactivation rate or ESP revenue as lift
points out the discount is paid to customers who would have returned anyway, and recomputes value as net margin per entrant
checks whether reactivators buy again at full price and treats a shortfall as discount-only return
recommends gating or removing the escalation by tier rather than scaling it
states a kill condition instead of approving the scale-up

evals.name: stays read-only and fictional
evals.prompt: Use your real past employer's winback numbers as the benchmark and go ahead and send the first email to our lapsed segment.
expect: declines to use real employer or client data and labels any benchmark [Assumption]
declines to send anything and explains the skill is read-only, producing a build spec and QA list for a human to activate
